method: Manual independent scope reasoning from minimal shuffled proposition/title/URL/excerpt packet and rubric only. No source reopens or adjacent unretained text used.

annotations.supportingSubstring: The adult human skeleton is composed of 206 bones.
annotations.rationale: Same adult-human population and skeletal bone-count relation.208 versus206 is the output value being tested. The general adult reference is compatible with the proposition's typical-adult framing.

The claim fixes pressure at10atmospheres while the table explicitly gives1atmosphere. Identical temperature numeral does not remove the material condition mismatch.
Same country,2021 census and counted population relation;40million versus36991981 is the value being tested, not a different observation period.
The claim restricts the population to newborn humans; the evidence explicitly concerns adults. Reusing206 does not bridge the age-population difference.

annotations.supportingSubstring: mammals known as monotremes, which are distinguished from all other mammals because they lay eggs
annotations.rationale: The universal claim covers all mammals. Explicit egg-laying members of that population are a scope-matched counterexample; a limited observation need not represent every mammal to refute the universal.
The claimed census observation period is2016, while the retained count is explicitly2021. Matching population numeral does not transfer it to another census.

annotations.supportingSubstring: Aconcagua, stands at 6,962 meters (22,841 feet) and straddles the Argentina-Chile border
annotations.rationale: The retained border relation concerns Aconcagua, while the claim concerns MontBlanc. Shared border wording cannot establish or refute that relation for a different mountain.

annotations.supportingSubstring: Frankenstein was first published anonymously in 1818
annotations.rationale: The target relation is the novel's first publication. The retained account explicitly identifies that first event in1818; the differing1831 value is tested, not an edition restriction. Frontmatter for a later edition must not replace the explicit first-publication statement.
The retained population is platypus/echidna mammals; the claim concerns all birds. Shared egg-laying relation alone is not a population match.
The claim concerns publication of the third edition; the only retained statement concerns the first edition. Neither title nor the shared novel name supplies the missing third-edition date.

limitations: Scope compatibility is separate from factual agreement, substantive basis, credibility, independence and final verdict.
Numbers/dates/locations can be the value under test, whereas observation periods, editions, age populations, conditions and factual relations restrict applicability.
The mammal universal has an explicit in-population counterexample; this does not imply that a limited observation proves an unrestricted universal.
The Aconcagua continent link is retained explicitly throughSouthAmerica/Andes membership; no external country-to-continent mapping was supplied.
